races.name: O'Donoghue Ring Collection Optional Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Useful form on good ground with three recent placed efforts, but a true hold-up horse by nature who will find himself racing in midfield rather than from the rear he needs; eight-year-old campaigner whose closing kick will be dulled by the compromised position.
runners_data.comment: Darkdeserthighway was below-par when unplaced last time out, but that followed back-to-back thirds and she rates strongly on our figures at 72, second of 14. Fit only 12 days off that run and proven at today's trip, she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Go Out
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form reads poorly with runs of 8-9-6 at this course and trip on good ground; lightly weighted but has yet to win or place in 12 career starts on similar going, making it hard to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Go Out heads our figures at 73, best-rated of the 14 here, despite a modest sequence of finishes no better than sixth in his last six starts. Fit from a run 27 days ago and proven at today's trip, the query is whether that figure holds up.

runners_data.name: Usuario Amigo
runners_data.note: One win and four places from 15 starts on similar ground gives him a solid course-going profile, but he is a natural closer who will be unable to get back to his preferred deep position in this hold-up-heavy field; Declan McDonogh takes over but the 1-day turnaround from his last start is an unusual flag.
runners_data.comment: Usuario Amigo backs up just a day after his last start and is proven at today's trip, with our figures rating him fourth of 14. He was ninth last time out and is winless in six, three of those runs unplaced, so he must find plenty.

runners_data.name: Elman
runners_data.note: Tagged as a fader in the finish and distance form over 12-16f suggests this trip is short of ideal; Denis Hogan runner on 15 days' rest but recent finishing positions of 10-11 on good ground offer little encouragement for a prominent challenge.
runners_data.comment: Elman sits down our figures in 12th of 14, and three unplaced efforts in his last five starts offer little encouragement. He does arrive fit having run 15 days ago and has form over today's trip, but the modest formline leaves plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Won last time over 8f on good ground at Killarney — directly relevant form — and a tongue-tie is fitted; prominent racing style suits the expected controlled pace perfectly, and Patrick McGettigan's 5lb claim adds appeal in an optional claimer.
runners_data.comment: Minaun View won last time out, her only success in six runs. She was runner-up earlier in that sequence too, though an eighth two starts back is the blot. Fit 12 days on and with today's trip proven, she holds fair claims from midfield on our figures at 67.

runners_data.name: Seti One
runners_data.note: Another Denis Hogan representative who fades in the finish and whose recent record shows 10-12-13 in three starts this season; hood fitted and goes on good ground but the finishing pattern is a significant negative.
runners_data.comment: Seti One has missed the frame in each of his last four starts, his best form a fourth-place effort further back. Fifth of 14 on our figures, he's fit from a run 15 days ago and proven at today's trip, but must rediscover that level to feature.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on good ground earlier in the season and placed twice at this trip, giving him a solid form profile; prominent style suits this shape well, and Adam Caffrey's booking for the McGuinness yard — who also saddle Minaun View — suggests dual-pronged attack.
runners_data.comment: Land Of The Giants was third last time out and has a win among his last six starts, form that reads better than his ninth-of-14 rank on our figures suggests. Fit 12 days on and with today's trip proven, he looks capable of building on that placing.

runners_data.name: Timandi
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 12f on good ground, but that longer trip and natural hold-up tendency make this sharp 8f on a turning track a different challenge; Luke McAteer rides but the horse will be stuck in midfield rather than its preferred rearward berth, compromising the usual late delivery.
runners_data.comment: Timandi won last time out, her only success in six runs. Two starts back she finished fourth, and the speed figure is stronger than her rank of 10th of 14 suggests. Fit just eight days on and with today's trip proven, she looks capable of building on that latest success.

runners_data.name: Aurora Mist
runners_data.note: Has a win on good ground over 8f to her name and showed a placed effort on similar; a genuine closer by inclination who will be pushed into midfield by the glut of hold-up types, though at 71 days since her last run freshness could be an asset if she handles the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Aurora Mist won last time out, her best form in a spell that also shows a seventh and two fifths, but that success came 71 days ago. Eleventh of 14 on our figures and with today's trip proven, the lengthy absence since is the obvious question mark.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the ride for Mrs Harrington, which is an obvious upgrade in quality; prominent style suits the anticipated race shape and a win over 10f on good ground this season suggests stamina is not a question, while the hood worn previously has been removed.
runners_data.comment: Glamazon was fourth last time out. She won four starts back, form that backs up her sixth-of-14 rating here. The yard is out of form of late though, just one winner from 31 runners in the last fortnight, a query alongside a modest eighth two starts back.

runners_data.name: Hazrama
runners_data.note: OR of 120 stands out as a numerical anomaly in this OR=60s field but finishing positions of 19th and 10th in only two career starts tell a sobering story; Chris Hayes rides but the fading-in-finish tag and very limited experience make this a difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: Hazrama sits bottom of our figures on 44, some way below this field, and has been unplaced in each of her last two starts. She has experience over today's trip and is fit from a run 18 days ago, but little in the formline suggests she can trouble this line-up.

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning, style listed as unknown, and Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking is the key positive in what otherwise looks a mid-division plodder; four placed efforts from six starts on good ground show she competes, but a win has not come yet.
runners_data.comment: Love Orchid has stayed frame-adjacent but no better, fourth to ninth across her last five starts with a fourth four back her best. Eighth of 14 on our figures and fit 14 days on, though the yard has landed just one from 21 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Magna Kotcha
runners_data.note: Tagged as a fader in the finish and three-run career record of 6-10-19 gives no platform for optimism; 87 days since last run adds an extra question mark, and Ben Coen's booking cannot paper over the weak form.
runners_data.comment: Magna Kotcha is second-bottom on our figures at 54, unplaced in each of her last two starts after a sixth three back, and has not run for 87 days. The yard is out of form too, landing just one from 21 in the last fortnight, leaving only experience over today's trip in her favour.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Funk
runners_data.note: Colin Keane for G M Lyons is the key booking and the horse is the only confirmed front-runner in the field, giving him a golden opportunity to control the pace; style-fit note flags a mild discount if the shape turns chaotic, but in a well-judged solo lead he is the one to beat.
runners_data.comment: Cosmic Funk was a close second two starts back, form that stands out in this field and underpins our selection despite a below-par seventh last time out. Fit from a run 27 days ago and proven at today's trip, that runner-up effort is the type of form this race needs.

races.paceDynamic: Cosmic Funk is the one confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no serious challenger for the lead, Colin Keane should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this mile on good ground at Killarney. The prominent types — Go Out, Minaun View, Land Of The Giants and Glamazon — will track close behind, but none of them has the profile or the mandate to force a contested early pace, meaning the tempo is likely to be honest rather than brutal. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Darkdeserthighway, Usuario Amigo, Timandi and Aurora Mist are genuine closers by inclination but will be shuffled into mid-division rather than finding their natural deep position, which blunts their finishing weapons. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to Cosmic Funk's controlled pace and pick up in the straight, as the truly held-up runners are compromised by the congested midfield they will be forced to race in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cosmic Funk Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Cosmic Funk is allowed to roll along uncontested and sets a steady, well-judged pace that suits those racing just off him.
scenarios.body: Keane dictates from the front without pressure, and the race becomes a test of which prominent tracker has the best turn of foot in the straight; horses who have been able to conserve energy close to the pace are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just slow enough to set up a sprint finish that catches Cosmic Funk slightly flat-footed in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The prominent mid-packers — Minaun View, Land Of The Giants and Glamazon — arrive with a joint challenge as the field fans out, and a horse with fresh legs and a good turn of foot from that second-rank position collects.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quick enough to string out the field and one of the nominally midfield closers — Timandi or Aurora Mist — finds a gap to deliver a genuine late run.
scenarios.body: Despite racing out of their ideal rearward role, a strong-finishing type that has been able to avoid traffic in a strung-out field can reel in the leaders close home; Aurora Mist's course form on good ground gives her the best profile here among this group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a moderate pace causes crowding and interference in the straight, gifting an unfancied runner a clear passage at the right moment.
scenarios.body: In a messy finish where the fancied horses block each other, a lightly-weighted runner like Love Orchid or Go Out finds daylight and capitalises; this is the least likely shape but the field's traffic problems in midfield make some interference plausible.

watchPoints.text: Cosmic Funk: watch whether Keane elects to roll along at a genuine clip or sits in behind — if he is absent from the front early the entire race shape changes and prominent stalkers inherit the race on their own terms.

Minaun View and Land Of The Giants: both McGuinness runners share the same race, so watch for stable tactics — if one is sent forward as a pace-pressure horse to soften things for the other, the dynamic shifts materially.

Usuario Amigo: the 1-day turnaround from last start is unusual and worth monitoring in the parade ring — if there is any sign of below-par condition, the compromised midfield position becomes an even bigger disadvantage.

Redistribution traffic — Darkdeserthighway, Timandi and Aurora Mist: all genuine closers who will be racing in midfield; watch the early stages to see whether any of them is nudged further back to reclaim a truer hold-up spot, as that would be a positive sign for their finishing prospects.

races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Race

runners_data.name: Dakota Jack
runners_data.comment: Unraced gelding making his debut here, so this is all about what he shows on the day. Carries 134 lb from draw 4 - unexposed and impossible to assess on form alone.

runners_data.name: South Dakota
runners_data.comment: Twice fourth in two starts, without a win yet, but he returns 27 days after his latest run and has raced over today's distance before. Ranked third of six on our figures with a strong speed figure, he looks capable of finishing closer this time.

runners_data.name: Venetian Power
runners_data.comment: Fourth on his only start so far, without a win yet, he returns 18 days later from a yard in red-hot form (17 from 51 in a fortnight) and has raced over today's distance before. Tops our figures here, making him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Full Volume
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after finishing sixth on his previous start, form on an upward curve. Returns 12 days later having raced over today's distance before, though the yard is out of form and he's only fourth of six on our figures.

runners_data.name: Pints Of Glory
runners_data.comment: Unraced colt making his debut, carrying 126 lb from draw 3. Lightly raced and totally unexposed, so this first sight of him will tell us plenty about his true form.

runners_data.name: Celtic Moon
runners_data.comment: Won last time out having finished fourth on her previous start, solid recent form. Returns 13 days later, has raced over today's distance before, and sits second of six on our figures, though the modest speed figure is the one query.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF Cairn Rouge Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Cromac Quay
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Mrs Harrington and Shane Foley, placed twice at a mile on good ground and clearly suited by conditions; solid each-way profile if the stalkers land a clean run.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after finishing runner-up and third before that, solid recent form. But our figures rate her below her official mark, only tenth of 12, and the yard is out of form after a 34-day break, though she has raced over today's distance before.

runners_data.name: Donna Time
runners_data.note: Unclassified style and modest OR of 74 makes her a significant outsider at this level; recent form of 7-6-2 shows a brief uptick but coming back from 10f to 1m on unknown going tests her range.|
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, a step up on the sixth and seventh before that, though still without a win. Our figures rate her second-bottom of 12 with a modest speed figure, but she returns quickly 11 days later having raced over today's distance before.

runners_data.name: Drop Dead Gorgeous
runners_data.note: AP O'Brien prominent type who won over this exact course-and-distance combination on soft; tongue-tie fitted, Lordan takes the ride, and a return to 1m brings her back to her winning trip — a legitimate each-way threat.|
runners_data.comment: She won four starts back, and backed that up with a third next time, before fading through this sequence to fifth last time out. Ranked fourth of 12 on our figures with a strong speed figure, though that below-par effort 38 days ago is the one query.

runners_data.name: Green Carrera
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone leader who has won three of her last four starts at a mile on good ground; Joseph O'Brien trains, McMonagle rides, and the absence of a rival to pressurise her suits, though the quality of the stalkers makes a hard hold essential.|
runners_data.comment: Won her last two starts, and three of her last five overall - clearly progressive form. She returns from a yard in red-hot form and has raced over today's distance before, marking her out as our selection on profile and fitness alone.

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's progressive filly has won four of her last five — all at seven furlongs — and steps up to a mile here for the first time; if she handles the trip she arrives in the best current form in the race, but the stamina question is real.|
runners_data.comment: Won each of her last four starts, with only a sixth and an unplaced effort further back in the sequence - the weight of wins stands out. Yet our figures rate her only eighth of 12, below her official mark of 97, though she returns 18 days on having raced over today's distance.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: Murphy's hold-up operator with a win at seven furlongs on good ground; at OR 100 she is the highest-rated runner, but 52 days off and a need for a decent pace to close into make her reliant on race conditions she may not get.|
runners_data.comment: She won five starts back and has had more good efforts since, and she tops our figures by some margin - the one to beat on that alone. A below-par eighth last time out is the outlier, though the 52-day gap since is a slight concern.

runners_data.name: Quiet Mutiny
runners_data.note: Twomey has had three winners in 14 days and this filly is a natural front-runner; squeezed back to a mapped midfield position because of the crowded prominent contingent, she will find it harder than usual to travel in her preferred spot — style-fit is discounted accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: She won four starts back, and was runner-up next time. Form then dipped to a fourth, before she was unplaced last time out. She still rates fifth of 12 on our figures and has raced over today's distance before, with room to bounce back 26 days on.

runners_data.name: Sinmara
runners_data.note: Second JP O'Brien runner, prominent by style but winless on good ground in recent starts; 52 days off, no headgear change, and an OR of 94 in a competitive field leaves her with plenty to prove.|
runners_data.comment: She won three starts back, and franked that with a fourth next time, before a below-par seventh last time out. From a yard in red-hot form, she ranks third of 12 on our figures with a strong speed figure, but the 52-day gap since is the one query.

runners_data.name: Sky Watch
runners_data.note: Unclassified style with hind-eye blinkers fitted; historical form shown in hurdle distances is an anomaly, and flat form at this trip and going is thin — hard to assess with confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, with a win two starts further back among a mixed sequence of finishes. She carries no figure from us this time round, so remains something of an unknown quantity, and she returns 45 days after her latest run.

runners_data.name: Spinning Around
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's filly is a genuine prominent racer who broke her maiden over seven furlongs on good ground, but forced into a midfield slot she cannot naturally exploit her front-running tendency; tongue-tie worn, style-fit tempered.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins among her last five starts, but her latest effort was a well-beaten eighth, having won two starts before that. She ranks seventh of 12 on our figures, leaving a mixed profile that could go either way.

runners_data.name: White Sand Beach
runners_data.note: AP O'Brien hold-up type running just two days after her last start, which is an unusually tight turnaround; placed consistently at a mile on good ground but has never won, and the blinkered hold-up profile needs a pace she is unlikely to get.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in each of her last two starts, without a win in six tries, though the placed form is at least consistent. She backs up quickly, just two days after that latest second, and has raced over today's distance before, but our figures only rank her ninth of 12.

runners_data.name: Wild Bessie
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's filly won at seven furlongs at Naas but fades in finishes and has been out 72 days; a natural front-runner who cannot get the position she needs in this field, and the fade flag compounds the concern over her effectiveness here.|
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, though she won two starts back and had a below-par run before that - mixed form in this sequence. She sits sixth of 12 on our figures with a strong speed figure and has raced over today's distance before, though the 72-day absence since is a concern.

races.paceDynamic: Green Carrera is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard, will stride into a clear lead from the outset and dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Killarney's flat mile. With Quiet Mutiny, Wild Bessie, and Spinning Around all natural prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred berth, there will be jostling early for the limited positions behind Green Carrera, though none are likely to seriously pressurise the leader's tempo. Meriden, Drop Dead Gorgeous, and Cromac Quay are the genuine prominent types most likely to slot in cleanly behind the pacesetter and travel comfortably in the slipstream throughout. This race shape — a lone leader setting an honest but unforced gallop — strongly favours prominent racers who can stalk the pace through the turn and produce a sustained finish, rather than hold-up horses who will need a significant gear-change that this tempo is unlikely to generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stalkers Pounce On Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Green Carrera sets a controlled lead and prominent stalkers track comfortably before overwhelming her in the straight.
scenarios.body: Green Carrera dictates a honest but unhurried pace, and the horses sitting second to fourth into the home turn have first use of the rail and the momentum to overpower her; Meriden's hat-trick of wins and strong Killarney-like flat-track form make her the prototype beneficiary, with Drop Dead Gorgeous also ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Green Carrera's gallop is truly unchallenged and her class advantage allows her to quicken clear when asked in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to pressurise her early, Green Carrera conserves energy and simply extends when shaken up; her three wins at this trip on good ground and a high STYLE_FIT for front-running make this credible, though the quality of the stalkers behind makes a solo win the second-most likely shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fast enough to cause attrition and the hold-up horses find daylight in time.
scenarios.body: Pivotal Attack is the one genuine hold-up type with strong going suitability and a useful win over seven furlongs on good ground; however, a lone moderate leader rarely generates the end-to-end gallop that typically sets up a late closer, making this the third-order shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the jostling prominent types disrupt the early order and the race devolves into a messy, uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: With Quiet Mutiny, Wild Bessie, and Spinning Around all racing out of their preferred role and potentially crowding the middle pack, erratic mid-race fractions could open the door to an unconventional winner; however, since those horses are not true hold-up types despite their mapped positions, this scenario depends on a false race that the likely field management makes improbable.

watchPoints.text: Green Carrera — if McMonagle is able to slide straight to the front unchallenged inside the first two furlongs, the lone-leader scenario immediately becomes live and the race could be over sooner than the odds suggest.

Meriden — watch whether Chris Hayes pushes her forward into second or third early; if she handles the step up to a mile and tracks the leader smoothly, her four-from-five form makes her the most dangerous individual in the field.

Pivotal Attack — Gary Carroll will need to find a clear passage from the hold-up position and a sufficient gallop to close into; if the pace is pedestrian her finish will be blunted and her market position could be misleading.

Quiet Mutiny, Wild Bessie, Spinning Around — monitor the first two furlongs for interference or crowding as three horses who want to race prominently are mapped back into midfield; any traffic trouble early is most likely to originate from this cluster.

Meriden's stamina — she has never raced beyond seven furlongs, so watch whether she is still travelling comfortably as the field rounds the home turn; if she weakens late it confirms a trip concern that would reshape the market for her next start.

races.name: Executive Helicopters Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with a win and two places from seven good-ground starts; travels well but needs a clear run in the final furlong — Sam Coen's claim is an asset and she ran just three days ago which bears monitoring.

runners_data.name: Jasmine Affanalis
runners_data.note: Has placed twice in eight good-ground starts including a win, and Luke McAteer is a strong booking; she races from off the pace and the step back to a mile after a string of shorter trips looks a sensible move.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who carries a headgear flag (visor) and a worrying fade pattern in recent finishes; good-going form is acceptable across distance but the finishing line tends to come too soon for him.

runners_data.name: Convincing
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been absent 107 days and steps back dramatically from trips of 10-16 furlongs to one mile — the distance drop is sharp and the layoff adds risk, though if fit he could sit just off Pete's Dream comfortably.

runners_data.name: Pete's Dream
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and only horse rated 0.90 for style fit; he has won over this trip on good ground before, but the system flags he is racing slightly out of natural role and the apprentice rider Jimmy Dalton adds a small unknown.

runners_data.name: James Henry
runners_data.note: Prominent-travelling type with three placings from five good-ground starts; the tongue-tie is worn again and Gavin Ryan's experience gives him the tactical edge to sit second or third and challenge late — 35 days since last run is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent recent form frequency (11 from 13 good-ground starts in the frame); wears blinkers, ran just six days ago, and a record of 0 wins in those 11 efforts is a caution, but Chris Hayes is a strong pilot.

runners_data.name: The Blue Panther
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature, placed on good ground twice from seven starts; shown in midfield on the map purely because the field is over-loaded with closers — Nicola Burns takes a valuable 5lb claim but the style-fit flag (0.92) tempering confidence is warranted.

runners_data.name: Tortola
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer with a fade pattern flagged, placed once from ten starts; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a top-class booking that partially offsets the concern, but the map position does not reflect his true rearward style and he needs pace to chase.

runners_data.name: Secret Magician
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type wearing blinkers with modest recent form (0 wins, 1 place from 15 good-ground attempts); Colin Keane lifts the booking quality significantly, though the 0.92 style-fit flag and thin form make this a minor player.

runners_data.name: Shahada Ace
runners_data.note: Has a fade pattern noted and a sequence of single-figure finishes in recent outings; the true hold-up position is masked by redistribution (style-fit 0.93), and a 10lb apprentice in Feenagh Moran riding her first or early winners makes this a risky proposition.

runners_data.name: Liamo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been off 45 days and carries headgear (tongue-strap and pad); shown in midfield on the map due to field congestion at the rear rather than natural preference — Paddy Harnett's 5lb claim is a mild plus but the layoff and headgear changes add uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Draiocht
runners_data.note: Has been off a very long 268 days and carries a hood; a winner on soft ground, she has never managed a place on good ground in five attempts — the style-fit flag (0.91) and extreme absence make this one of the most speculative runners in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Pete's Dream is the lone confirmed front-runner and is likely to slot into a comfortable lead from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop over this flat mile without any genuine pressure from behind. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Bella Colombia, Jasmine Affanalis, Medieval Night, The Blue Panther, Tortola, Secret Magician, Shahada Ace, Liamo, and Draiocht all want to come from off the pace — meaning the contested section of this race is largely in the latter stages rather than from the break. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; The Blue Panther, Tortola, Shahada Ace, and Secret Magician are the most likely to actually push forward into midfield positions to secure better ground, but they are not natural front-runners and will not pressurise Pete's Dream meaningfully. With a lone pace-setter dictating an uncontested, measured tempo over a flat mile, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a sustained late run — those with genuine finishing kick and a clean passage to the outside will be the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If Pete's Dream dictates a steady, uncontested pace and the hold-up brigade cannot generate enough late momentum on a soft-enough tempo.
scenarios.body: Pete's Dream sets a relaxed gallop and simply quickens away from the field in the final two furlongs before the closers can organise a challenge; the prominent types James Henry and Convincing, travelling in second and third, are best placed to pounce if the leader flags.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that a well-timed hold-up run from the back produces a late surge in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A measured tempo sets up a sprint finish and the horses with the most tractable closing runs — Bella Colombia and Jasmine Affanalis — find the rail or widest route to deliver; their good-going form at this trip makes them best equipped to finish off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Convincing or James Henry push forward aggressively early and sustain their effort to deny the hold-up horses a clean run.
scenarios.body: Either Convincing or James Henry tracks Pete's Dream closely and presses from the two-furlong pole, turning it into a slog that rewards those who travel prominently rather than those making late runs; the hold-up horses lose ground in traffic and cannot pick up in time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed horses push forward from their unnatural midfield positions and inject a messy mid-race surge.
scenarios.body: Tortola, The Blue Panther, or Secret Magician push up unexpectedly to crowd the pace, fracturing the race shape and creating a more attritional contest that suits horses with stamina reserves; this chaotic shape remains unlikely given how passive this group of hold-up horses has been in recent form.

watchPoints.text: Pete's Dream is entirely unchallenged on the front end — watch whether Jimmy Dalton (7lb claimer) settles him conservatively or lets him stride clear early, as that choice will determine whether the hold-up horses can close at all.

Convincing has been off 107 days and drops sharply in trip from 10-16 furlongs; if he travels strongly for Ben Coen and gets a prominent pitch he could be dangerous, but fitness on first run back after a long break is the key question.

Medieval Night ran just six days ago — watch his behaviour in the paddock and early in the race for signs of a quick turnaround taking its toll, as he has placed frequently but not won in 11 good-ground starts.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Tortola, The Blue Panther, Secret Magician, Shahada Ace) may all attempt to push forward in the early stages; if three or four of them move up simultaneously they could accidentally press Pete's Dream and turn a steady race into a contested one.

Draiocht returns from 268 days off with a hood applied for the first time in a handicap — an abnormally long absence combined with new headgear on good ground (a surface on which she is 0 from 5) makes her a live drifter to monitor in the market.

runners_data.name: Vervain

runners_data.name: Alto Sax

runners_data.name: Monroe Dasher

races.paceDynamic: Tassarolo is the only confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field and, with no obvious challenger for the lead, Chris Hayes should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m3½f trip on good ground. Behind the pacesetter, Deuteronomy and Limestone Red are the likeliest to press into prominent positions, but the bulk of the field — Limbocall, Vervain, Alto Sax, Voice Of Northeast, Highway Sixty One, Monroe Dasher, Crypto Crash, and Fantasy Fara — are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is no room for all of them at the rear in practice. With Tassarolo setting a measured, uncontested tempo, the race is unlikely to produce a strong enough gallop to stretch the field out and deliver a true staying test; instead, a bunch finish is plausible with those racing close to the pace enjoying the clearest run. This shape favours horses who can travel prominently or in a handy midfield position and produce a sustained finishing effort — pure hold-up horses who need a strong pace to aid their late run are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tassarolo Controls, Pace Suits Handy Types
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo leads at a fair but uncontested clip and those sitting just off the pace get first run.
scenarios.body: Hayes on Tassarolo sets a comfortable tempo that compresses the field, and horses like Deuteronomy and Young Churchill, travelling smoothly in behind, get the clearest passage into the straight and simply outlast rivals from a handy berth.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slow Crawl, Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo is allowed to set a truly dawdling early pace and kicks clear in the straight before closers can respond.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian gallop with no pressure from behind turns the race into a sprint for home with Tassarolo already lengths clear; the hold-up horses redistributed to midfield are in no-man's-land and lack the finishing speed to peg back a front-runner who has stolen a march.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Best Horse Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out and those tracking from midfield produce the best sustained effort.
scenarios.body: A fair gallop creates a proper stamina test and runners who have genuine staying form over this sort of trip pick their way through; Alto Sax's recent good-ground form and Kevin The Great's better efforts at this distance make them dangers if they can get a clear passage from their midfield berth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entering the straight, creating a wall of horses and leaving the door open for a late swooper.
scenarios.body: This depends on redistributed hold-up horses genuinely getting to the rear and benefiting from a strong enough pace to make late ground — both conditions are unlikely given the compressed field and Tassarolo's uncontested lead; Arch Enemy, who has winning form on good ground, is the most credible late threat if the scenario materialises.

watchPoints.text: Tassarolo's early lead is the race's key variable — watch whether Chris Hayes is allowed to stride into an uncontested advantage or if Deuteronomy and Limestone Red push up to apply any early pressure.

Colin Keane on Limbocall and Ben Coen on Alto Sax are the two highest-profile jockey bookings among the redistributed hold-up horses — if either gets a clean early position rather than being forced wide or back, they could outrun their mapped roles.

God Of Thunder's known finishing fade is a significant concern in a race where the pace may be slow enough to compress the field — watch whether Daniel King elects to ride more prominently than the horse's usual style to counteract this tendency.

Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking on Highway Sixty One is a market watch — if this horse drifts or shortens significantly at the off, it could signal stable confidence in a runner whose recent 12f good-ground placed effort gives him a legitimate each-way profile.

With going listed as unknown throughout the card, any late market moves triggered by a ground report closer to race time should be treated as significant, particularly for horses like Vervain and Fantasy Fara whose form figures vary sharply between good and soft.

runners_data.name: Celestially

runners_data.comment: A third-placed effort stands out in a modest run of finishes across her last five starts, and she does have experience over today's trip. A speed figure of 71 is workable, but a rating of 63 - 13th of 14 - leaves her fighting a big weight of numbers under 119 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Lagoon Nebula is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 14-horse field and, with no genuine rival likely to press from the outset, should dictate at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m6½f trip on good ground at Killarney. Baila Conmigo, Coulstys Way, Jurality, and Folly Beach are the legitimate prominent types capable of tracking in second through fourth, giving the leader a small, organised group ahead of a large hold-up pack. The field holds more hold-up and midfield types than the map can accurately place at the rear — Sonic Invader, Maarisha, Parish Express, Lauderdale King, and Celestially are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to the midfield tier on the map, meaning the rear of the race will be even more congested than shown; of these, Sonic Invader and Maarisha are best-credentialled to secure a workable position. With one uncontested pace-setter controlling an honest but unfrantic gallop, this race shape primarily rewards horses that travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final quarter-mile — prominent racers with proven good-ground form at this trip hold the clearest structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lagoon Nebula Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lagoon Nebula dictates a comfortable solo lead and the prominent group behind lack the will or ability to close the gap.
scenarios.body: Lagoon Nebula sets a measured fractions over 1m6½f on an unchallenged lead and still has enough in reserve to repel challengers entering the straight; the prominent trackers Jurality and Baila Conmigo, travelling just off the pace, are ideally placed to capitalise if the leader weakens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace set by Lagoon Nebula proves just slow enough that the second-rank prominent horses sustain their momentum and run past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Jurality and Baila Conmigo, having saved ground racing prominently, find a genuine late gear while Lagoon Nebula ties up after controlling throughout; this suits horses with demonstrated staying form at the trip on good ground who can race handily without being exposed to a searching gallop early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely searching enough that the early leaders tie up and a well-positioned midfield horse picks up the pieces inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Sonic Invader and Moyassr, whose recent form shows placed efforts at staying trips on good ground, have the profile to deliver a late run if gap-finding is straightforward; however, the field's true hold-up horses have been pushed back into an already-crowded mid-division, reducing the likelihood that a clean late run materialises freely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race Suits Dark Horse
scenarios.trigger: If early positional jostling among the prominent group disrupts the pace pattern and creates an unpredictable finish that scrambles the expected order.
scenarios.body: A chaotic fractions scenario with multiple prominent types competing for position behind Lagoon Nebula could leave several fancied runners in trouble while a fresh or lightly raced runner catches rivals flat-footed; Party Dress and Celestially, with fitness queries but latent ability, are the types who might benefit from disorder, though neither holds strong structural claims in a settled race.

watchPoints.text: Jurality (W.J. Lee) tracked a strong pace to win at 13f on good ground recently and has placed twice more over this trip range — if he travels smoothly in second or third, he is the primary threat to any race leader in the straight.

Sonic Invader's Colin Keane booking is significant given the horse's back-to-back 3rd-place efforts at 16f and 14f on good — watch whether Keane can negotiate a forward enough position from a likely congested mid-to-rear group, as clean running will be the difference between placed and winning.

Maarisha returns after 267 days absent with Gavin Ryan aboard — a market move on the exchanges pre-race would suggest the stable is confident about fitness, and this horse's natural style means it needs a strong gallop to deliver; monitor the market closely.

Lagoon Nebula's early position will set the entire complexion of the race — if Luke McAteer sends promptly to the front and immediately controls the fractions, the pace remains sustainable and front-rank types are favoured; any hesitation in front could invite Baila Conmigo or Coulstys Way to press the pace and change the dynamic.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Sonic Invader, Parish Express, Lauderdale King, Celestially) competing for identical ground in a 14-runner field creates a significant interference risk on the home turn — watch for scrimmaging in the rear half of the field from 3f out.
